notes.hodi: Called at the door. The answer is Karibu!

guidebook.intro: Good manners open every door on the coast and inland. A few words and gestures show people you respect them.

tips.title: Asking politely
body: **Naomba** (I ask for) is much softer than **Nataka** (I want). Use it in shops, at a friend’s home and with anyone older: **Naomba chai**.
At a door, call **Hodi!** and wait for **Karibu!** before you go in. Greet elders first with **Shikamoo**, and wait for **Marahaba**.

culture.title: The right hand
body: Give, receive and eat with the **right hand**, or with both hands to show extra respect. Using only the left hand can seem rude.
**Pole kwa kazi** is said to anyone working, from a cook to a builder: it recognises their effort.
